author: NewsBreak
title: California Leads Legal Push to Protect School Mental Health Funds Under Threat from Federal Cuts - NewsBreak
text: OAKLAND — California Attorney General Rob Bonta is taking a stand against the Trump Administration’s attempt to cut mental health support in schools. From Oakland, Bonta announced that California, alongside a coalition of 16 other states, has filed a motion in federal court to block the U.S. Department of Education from pulling the plug on key school mental health grant programs that provide millions in funding to education agencies across the state. The motion, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, seeks to prevent the Department from halting the Mental Health Service Professional Demonstration Grant Program and the School-Based Mental Health Services Grant Program. These initiatives fund local school districts, universities, and county education offices throughout California, with roughly $200 million already awarded, according to Bonta’s office. In a statement from Oakland, Bonta emphasized the impact this loss would have across the state. “The Trump Administration’s Department of Education should be focused on supporting the success and education of our students, but instead they are using flimsy and unlawful excuses to rip funding from projects that support the mental health and well-being of our students,” said Bonta. “The loss of this funding would cause immense harm to California students, especially in our low-income and rural communities.” The dispute began on April 29, 2025, when the Department issued generic letters to grantees, including institutions in Los Angeles, Fresno, and San Bernardino, stating their funding would not continue. The letters cited vague new priorities, such as “merit, fairness, and excellence in education,” with no explanation for why specific programs were cut. According to the complaint, the Department also admitted that it targeted states whose grant proposals included diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts—a move the states argue is legally indefensible. Back in June, Bonta and the multistate coalition filed a lawsuit to challenge the Department’s decision, arguing it violates federal law. In yesterday’s move, Bonta asked the court to issue a preliminary injunction that would keep the grants flowing while the legal battle unfolds.
